analysis: The only change in this PR (docs/provider/cli-reference.md, head lines ~1756-1758 per the patch) adds three rows to the environment-variable forwarding table: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS. Each row cites a source constant in GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift or EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift. The supplied units (head lines 1-404 and 405-824) contain none of the changed lines, because the diff lies beyond the excerpt. I therefore reviewed only the surrounding documentation, which describes existing behavior: the cache set/status commands, logout token revocation, the App Attest enroll guidance, and the drain and switch flows. I found nothing in this text that weakens an existing control, and no security-relevant behavior change visible in the supplied lines. The documented env variables are TTFT-related tuning knobs for idle cache sweep, segment retention and host zeros. These could plausibly relate to T-028 (residual GPU/KV data) or the T-041 prefix-cache surface, depending on semantics. Neither the Swift sources nor the semantics are supplied, so I cannot tell whether they change KV retention or zeroing, nor whether they are forwarded into launchd. Question for integration: confirm that these knobs (especially SEGMENT_RETENTION and SEGMENT_HOST_ZEROS) do not weaken KV memory clearing or the encrypted prefix-cache TTL, disk budget and kill-switch posture, and that the 'forwarded' table entry matches the code. This is a documentation-only change with no demonstrated regression, so I report no findings.
